comparison: Both evaluate the NR2F2 expression pattern characterization (C1-C24). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of immunofluorescence data quality and notes the correlative nature of progenitor identification. Peer reviewers unanimously praised data quality as 'beautiful' and 'well presented' with proper controls and statistics.

OpenEval evaluates RUNX1 expression and interstitial progenitor identification (C4-C7). Peer R1 covers these claims within the broader expression pattern evaluation (C1-C24), accepting all findings without specific comment on these particular claims.

Both evaluate Wt1CreERT2 knockout phenotypes (C25-C31). OpenEval notes the kidney phenotype may complicate testis-specific interpretation. Peer reviewers accepted all findings, with Reviewer 1 confirming 'major reduction in FLC numbers' and undescended testis.

Both evaluate FLC differentiation defects in Wt1CreERT2 mutants (C32-C40). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of quantification rigor. Peer reviewers unanimously accepted findings, with Reviewer 1 noting both genetic systems showed 'undescended testis and major reduction in FLC numbers.'

Both evaluate testis cord morphology defects (C41-C47). OpenEval assesses morphometric quantification and ACTA2 expression data. Peer R2 covers these claims within broader Wt1CreERT2 phenotype evaluation (C25-C51), accepting all findings.

Both evaluate the distinction between specification and differentiation defects (C48-C51). OpenEval notes this is reasonable interpretation though could benefit from earlier timepoint analysis. Peer reviewers accepted this conclusion without challenge.

Both evaluate Sertoli cell phenotypes in Wt1CreERT2 mutants (C52-C57). OpenEval notes importance for interpreting potential non-cell-autonomous effects. Peer reviewers specifically praised this analysis, with Reviewer 2 highlighting the 'great rigor' in interpreting confounding Wt1 haploinsufficiency effects.

Both evaluate the Wt1CreERT2 haploinsufficiency control experiment (C58-C64). OpenEval notes this is critical for interpretation and motivates the Nr5a1-Cre model. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this rigor, with Reviewer 2 stating it 'demonstrates the great rigor with which the authors interpreted the results.'

Both evaluate Nr5a1-Cre characterization and expression pattern (C65-C76). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the characterization thoroughness. Peer reviewers endorsed this second genetic system, with Reviewer 2 praising the use of two different conditional systems demonstrating the same effects.

Both evaluate Sertoli cell phenotypes in Nr5a1-Cre mutants (C77-C81). OpenEval notes this model avoids Sertoli defects seen with Wt1CreERT2, providing cleaner evidence. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of their endorsement of the Nr5a1-Cre system.

Both evaluate FLC reduction and cell-autonomous function in Nr5a1-Cre mutants (C82-C88). OpenEval notes 40% reduction is statistically significant and cell-autonomous conclusion is strengthened by absence of Sertoli defects. Peer reviewers confirmed both systems showed 'major reduction in FLC numbers.'

Both evaluate cryptorchidism and masculinization defects in Nr5a1-Cre mutants (C89-C94). OpenEval assesses the link between reduced hormone expression and phenotypes. Peer reviewers accepted these findings, with Reviewer 1 noting 'undescended testis' in both genetic models.

Both evaluate progenitor specification, proliferation, and survival (C99-C105). OpenEval notes this comprehensive analysis rules out these mechanisms and focuses attention on differentiation. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating 'NR2F2 has no effect on the amount and expression of the progenitor cells.'

Both evaluate reduced NR5A1 upregulation in mutants (C106-C107). OpenEval identifies this as a key mechanistic finding. Peer reviewers accepted this finding as part of the mechanistic analysis, though did not comment specifically on NR5A1.

Both evaluate DHH and PDGFRA pathway analysis (C108-C115, C117). OpenEval notes comprehensive pathway analysis provides strong evidence these pathways are not impaired. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed this, with Reviewer 1 confirming 'does not seem to affect other signalling pathways' and the editor highlighting NR2F2 acts 'without altering paracrine signals.'

Both evaluate endothelial cells and NOTCH signaling (C118-C126). OpenEval notes importance because increased endothelial/NOTCH can inhibit FLC differentiation. Peer reviewers accepted these findings, with Reviewer 1 specifically mentioning 'NOTCH pathway' is not affected.

Both evaluate the Bhmt control experiment ruling out adult Leydig cell identity (C127-C129). OpenEval notes this addresses an alternative hypothesis. Peer reviewers accepted this finding as part of the comprehensive maturation defect analysis.

Both evaluate reduced steroidogenic gene expression per FLC (C130-C134). OpenEval notes the normalization approach is appropriate but makes assumptions about HSD3B immunofluorescence. Peer reviewers accepted these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating mutants have 'less FLC and they are immature.'

Both evaluate immature FLC morphology (C135-C139). OpenEval assesses the morphometric analysis and interpretation based on prior literature. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as evidence of immaturity, with Reviewer 1 confirming FLCs 'are immature.'

Both evaluate the dual role conclusion (C140-C141). OpenEval notes this integrates multiple lines of evidence though molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Peer reviewers endorsed this conclusion, with the editor stating NR2F2 'helps to initiate the differentiation' and affects maturation 'until these cells mature into functional secretory cells.'

Both evaluate the sufficiency of partial FLC loss for cryptorchidism (C152). OpenEval notes this demonstrates threshold requirements for testis descent. Peer R8 covers this within the broader conclusion evaluation (C147-C155), accepting the overall findings.

Both evaluate the NR5A1 mechanism and integration with prior work (C158-C161). OpenEval notes reduced NR5A1 upregulation is directly observed and its sufficiency is supported by citations. Peer reviewers accepted the mechanistic model, with the editor noting NR2F2 'helps to initiate the differentiation.'

Both evaluate speculation about cooperating factors like ARX (C162-C164). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting it's speculative without direct evidence. Peer reviewers did not criticize this speculation, with Reviewer 1 praising the discussion for paving 'the way for several interesting follow up studies.'

Both evaluate comparison of FLC and ALC development (C165-C168). OpenEval notes this is supported by citations to prior work. Peer reviewers accepted this comparative discussion without objection, with Reviewer 1 praising the discussion section.

Both evaluate NR2F2 mechanisms in ALC models (C169-C171). OpenEval notes these are in vitro findings in ALC models rather than direct fetal evidence. Peer reviewers accepted this integration of published data without challenge.

Both evaluate maturation defect mechanisms and potential direct regulation (C172-C177). OpenEval notes the direct regulation hypothesis remains to be tested functionally. Peer reviewers accepted this discussion, with Reviewer 1 praising it for suggesting follow-up studies.

Both evaluate clinical relevance and human NR2F2 variants (C182-C193). OpenEval notes the connection is somewhat speculative given species differences and lack of direct human functional studies. Peer reviewers endorsed the translational relevance, with the editor noting the work 'will be of interest to colleagues studying reproductive development in mammals including humans.'

Peer R13 evaluates established background facts about FLC differentiation (C95-C98). No corresponding OpenEval result found - OpenEval did not separately evaluate background/introductory claims. Peer reviewers accepted these as properly supported by citations.

Peer R11 evaluates testis cord morphology observations (C178-C181). No corresponding OpenEval result found - these claims were not separately evaluated by OpenEval, though related morphology claims (C41-C47) were covered in OpenEval R5. Peer reviewers accepted morphological data as well presented.
